reason: Checked every path. add_zone_column: only entries are the four JSR/JMP in add_scroll_zone (render.6502:876/884/890/898), each directly after STA zone_tmp_hi, so A = zone_tmp_hi on entry; no label+N or other references. zone_tmp_hi is &0064 (ren_zp); the listing shows no other access to &64 (only the four STAs and the removed LDA), the IRQ does not touch it, and its new value (X) is dead after. zone_n is at most 4 (STZ at render.6502:369, two add_scroll_zone calls of two entries each; zone_lo/zone_hi SKIP 4), so INX never wraps and STA zone_hi-1,X / zone_lo-1,X hit the same bytes as before. zone_n now written before the list entries: only readers are span_in_zone and sky_edges.in_zone, both on the render path, not the interrupt. Exit state: X restored from &64 (same value), Y untouched, A clobbered (callers reload A / add_scroll_zone's caller does INY; CPY), and flags are in fact identical: N/Z from LDX of the same X as PLX gave, C and V untouched by every instruction in both versions. Stack: the old pushed one byte and popped it; the new uses none, so depth at RTS is the same and the IRQ only sees less stack use. span_in_zone: C = 0 at .each from the prefix (CLC; ADC #2 with A from mover_types_width_table indexed by type AND &7F: all 128 bytes &DA55-&DAD4 are <= &22, so no carry; STA/LDA/BNE/DEC zp/LDX/BEQ keep C), and from .next (BNE next after ADC #0 is taken only on a non-zero result, which cannot carry; BCS hit not taken means C = 0; TXA keeps C). With C = 0, SBC span_x_hi equals CLC; SBC span_x_hi, so span_d, span_d+1 and the result are unchanged. No outside reference to span_in_zone.each. Recount: add_zone_column 37 -> 33 cycles a call (-4), 17 -> 18 bytes; loop -2 cycles an iteration, -1 byte; net 0 bytes. The claim's 5 'per execution' mixes the two; per call of add_zone_column it is 4, plus 2 per span_in_zone zone iteration.
